---
Sunlight contains all colors of the visible spectrum, but as it enters Earth's atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules and scatters in all directions. Shorter wavelengths of light, like blue and violet, scatter much more strongly than longer wavelengths like red and orange—a phenomenon known as Rayleigh scattering. Although violet scatters even more than blue, our eyes are more sensitive to blue and the Sun emits less violet light, so the sky appears blue to us.
